outside_scope_open.reason: The historical standalone verifier retains stored-string artifact comparison; changing the producer does not remediate that historical copy.
The historical standalone verifier retains the previously identified unconditional report claims; it was not edited or executed.

limitations: All generation/verification execution used owned temporary roots/HOME and synthetic artifacts. No real Git, operator key, network publication, native/hardware effect or ATTESTED object was executed/generated.

Successful verification only establishes the declared selected-file byte integrity at observation time and, when an external key is supplied, software signature validity relative to that explicitly trusted key. It does not attest the whole repository, associate bytes with Git HEAD, certify suites, or establish hardware/operator identity.
Freshness uses local wall-clock age, not a trusted timestamp authority or an anti-replay ledger.
Portable verification requires its Python BLAKE3 dependency and cryptography for signature checks; executing verifier code still assumes that verifier implementation itself is trusted.
Per-file reads and normal failure cleanup were checked. No crash-atomic publication or immunity to a concurrent same-UID writer is claimed.
Historical signed materials were not regenerated. Legacy v1 input is intentionally refused by the new contract; historical v2 C0135/C0136 remain OPEN.
Parent-reported MyPy and broader related-suite outcomes are not represented as independently executed checks in this review.
